page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.96xlarge is a large-scale, general-purpose compute instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features Intel x86_64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, providing 384 dedicated virtual CPUs across 192 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). The instance is allocated 1536.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units, centering its design purely on dense CPU compute and high-capacity system memory.

A key architectural feature of the m8idn.96xlarge is its bundled local storage and high-speed networking subsystems. The system includes 22800 GB (22.8 TB) of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage, delivering high local disk throughput and low latency for operations that demand fast temporary data access. Networking performance is provisioned with 600 Gbps of baseline bandwidth, accommodating massive data transport volumes across cluster environments, distributed storage backends, and decoupled enterprise application tiers without network saturation.

The inclusion of massive NVMe storage alongside a high 600 Gbps network profile makes this instance architecturally effective for I/O-intensive and data-heavy environments. Qualitatively, consolidating high vCPU counts, extensive RAM, and dense local NVMe storage reduces inter-node communication overhead compared to distributing tasks across multiple smaller nodes. However, because local NVMe instance store volumes are ephemeral, workloads requiring long-term persistence must implement external replication or state management. The configuration is well suited for high-transaction distributed databases, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caches, distributed processing clusters, and enterprise-scale ETL workflows.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.96xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by Intel x86_64 processors clocked at 3.9 GHz. It provides 384 dedicated vCPUs across 192 physical cores alongside 1536 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU distribution. The instance features 22800 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage to support high-throughput, low-latency disk access directly on the host, complemented by 600 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. With no integrated GPUs, resource allocation focuses entirely on general-purpose compute density, large memory capacity, and high network and local disk throughput. These specifications make the m8idn.96xlarge well suited for running distributed databases, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines, enterprise applications, and high-concurrency real-time stream processing engines.
